answer: Picture the agent economy as a haven built on a knoll: every new identity must pay an entry toll funded from a traceable source, and the toll rises steeply when many identities draw from the same funding cluster - a falcon-eye view of the money graph spots the flock. A lone honest agent pays once and cheaply; a sybil farmer funding a thousand puppets pays a toll that compounds with each sibling, until forging the next identity costs more than any reward it could earn.
